answers.title: What mid-size companies ask about AI-ready data

items.a: AI-ready data is data that is accurate, consistent, well documented, governed and accessible enough for AI models and agents to use safely. It represents the business use case, carries clear definitions and lineage, and is monitored over time. Gartner predicts organizations will abandon 60% of AI projects unsupported by AI-ready data through 2026.

items.q: What does a data readiness assessment include?
items.a: A data readiness assessment profiles your critical data sources and scores them on quality, integration, governance, security and fit for priority AI and analytics use cases. TEAM International delivers the results as a Data Readiness Scorecard plus a prioritized remediation and modernization roadmap with effort and impact for each gap.

items.q: What is a good data modernization strategy?
items.a: A good data modernization strategy starts from business use cases, not technology. Assess the current state, fix the data quality issues that block priority use cases, integrate silos into a modern cloud data platform in phases, and put governance in place as you go. Each phase should deliver usable data products, not just infrastructure.

Data harmonization makes data from different systems consistent: the same customer, product or transaction is described with the same identifiers, formats and definitions everywhere. It combines cleansing, standardization, master data management and shared business definitions, and it is a prerequisite for reliable analytics and AI.

items.q: When do you need data governance consulting?
items.a: You need data governance consulting when teams don't trust reports, nobody owns key data, sensitive data is hard to control, or AI projects can't get approved because data risk is unclear. A practical governance program sets ownership, policies, a data catalog, lineage and access controls sized to your organization, not a heavy bureaucracy.

items.q: Can we get value from AI before our data is fully modernized?
items.a: Yes. TEAM International's Fast Track platform option connects to most existing systems and lets business users query enterprise data in natural language and build no-code AI agents within weeks. It runs alongside the data readiness roadmap, delivering early value and showing where data quality work matters most.

items.a: Data readiness is how prepared an organization's data is to support a specific goal, such as analytics, automation or AI. It covers data quality, integration, governance, security and documentation. TEAM International measures it with a data readiness assessment and a Data Readiness Scorecard, then closes the gaps that matter most.

items.q: How long does a data readiness assessment take?
items.a: A typical data readiness assessment takes three to four weeks for a defined set of priority use cases and data sources. It ends with a Data Readiness Scorecard and a prioritized remediation and modernization roadmap, so you can plan budget and sequence with facts.

items.q: What do your data modernization services include?
items.a: TEAM International's data modernization services cover enterprise data integration, pipeline and API development, migration from legacy warehouses to a modern cloud data platform on Microsoft Azure or AWS, and data platform modernization, delivered in phases tied to priority analytics and AI use cases.

items.q: What does data governance consulting include?
items.a: Our data governance consulting defines data ownership and stewardship, policies and standards, a data catalog and lineage, access control and privacy, and governance for AI use. We size the program to your organization so it improves trust without adding bureaucracy.

items.q: How do you improve data quality?
items.a: We apply a data quality framework: profile data to find errors, gaps and duplicates, fix them at the source where possible, standardize formats and definitions, set up master data for key entities, and add automated data quality checks and monitoring so quality stays high over time.

items.q: What is the Fast Track platform option?
items.a: The Fast Track platform option is a ready-to-use platform that connects to most enterprise data sources, lets business users ask questions in natural language, and lets teams build AI agents without code. It delivers value in weeks while the data readiness roadmap continues.

items.q: Do we need to replace our current data platform?
items.a: Usually not. Our data engineers work across Microsoft Azure and AWS, modernize around the platforms you already run, and replace only the components that block quality, scale or AI. The roadmap from the assessment shows what to keep, upgrade or retire.

items.q: How is data readiness different from an AI readiness assessment?
items.a: An AI readiness assessment looks at strategy, use cases, skills, governance and technology across the organization. A data readiness assessment goes deep on the data itself: quality, integration, governance and fitness for specific AI and analytics use cases. Many companies start with data readiness because data is the most common blocker.

items.q: Do you work with mid-size companies?
items.a: Yes. TEAM International has built enterprise data and software systems for more than 20 years and works with mid-size companies too. Senior teams, an assessment-first approach and the Fast Track option make data readiness affordable for mid-size budgets.

Start with a data readiness assessment. In three to four weeks, TEAM International scores your priority data sources and delivers a Data Readiness Scorecard and a remediation and modernization roadmap, so you can decide next steps with clear scope and cost.
